LESSON: CLASSIFICATION OF PLANTS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 1.1: Classification of Plants

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Classification of Plants
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: when handling plants as they study flowering and non- flowering plants. How are plants classified?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. classify plants into flowering and non- flowering
2. describe functions of parts of a flower
3. appreciate the importance of flowers in nature
4. describe general characteristics of vertebrates
5. classify vertebrates into their main groups

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Classification of Plants

Teach
• Observe Classification of Plants in real life (school compound, home, farm).
• Use safe examples only.
• Name → explain → apply.

Worked example
• Fact 1 about Classification of Plants (in pupil words).
• Fact 2 with a Kenyan example.
• Safe action connected to Classification of Plants.

Try this
• Draw/label one diagram for Classification of Plants.
• Write 5 bullet facts about Classification of Plants.
• Say one safety rule.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• classify plants into flowering and non- flowering
• describe functions of parts of a flower
• appreciate the importance of flowers in nature

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. List 8 facts on Classification of Plants.
2. Teach a friend using only bullet points.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet for Classification of Plants: meaning, diagram, 5 practice questions.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when handling plants as they study flowering and non- flowering plants. How are plants classified?
2. What are the key features of vertebrates?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• classify plants into flowering and non- flowering
• describe functions of parts of a flower
• appreciate the importance of flowers in nature
• describe general characteristics of vertebrates

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
